evidence_items.publisher: arXiv / Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton, and Owain Evans
evidence_items.explanation: TruthfulQA supports the narrower concern that tested language models reproduce common misconceptions. These earlier tests do not establish unavoidable reproduction across the tools discussed in March 2024 or prove unauthorized data provenance.
The training objective gives the autocomplete analogy a factual basis for GPT-4. It does not establish that this describes every generative tool or that inherited errors cannot be corrected.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph describing Firefly's first model and enterprise training
evidence_items.explanation: Adobe's disclosed sourcing challenges a universal claim that generative AI necessarily uses stolen material. It is a provider disclosure about an image model, not an independent provenance audit of the language models central to the passage.

unresolved_gaps: The cited studies do not trace specific unauthorized training examples into recurring mistakes across the relevant tools.
No comprehensive provenance record establishes the asserted unauthorized sourcing or petabyte quantity.
The evidence does not establish inevitability; the ordinary persistent-fallibility reading remains broader than the cited tests.
The scope changes materially depending on whether tools means language models or all generative AI.
